svg.title: 04 Personas
svg.desc: Who are we designing for, what do they do all day and where do they stand on handing work to an agent? Decisions fed: D-07, D-08. Status: Draft. Reconstructed for portfolio purposes; illustrative.

text.tspan: Question: Who are we designing for, what do they do all day and where do they stand on handing work to an agent?
I decided: Four composites cut by accountability, not by seniority alone, plus one anti-persona.
Role-based views of the same run came out of this cut.
We built: The cards from the coded material, with the evidence rows attached, reviewed in critique
by the whole design team.

svg.text: FOUR COMPOSITE PERSONAS AND ONE ANTI-PERSONA. COMPOSITE AND RECONSTRUCTED. EACH PERSONA IS A COMPOSITE BUILT FROM THE THEMES IN 03. NO ATTRIBUTE CARRIES AN OBSERVATION, PARTICIPANT OR QUOTE COUNT. NAMES ARE INVENTED.

text.tspan: Fourth busy season. Runs fieldwork on three
engagements at once.
Client site three days a week, laptop on a
shared table, calls interrupting. Firm office
or home the other two.
- Get every sample traced and every exception
explained before the manager's review slot.
- Hand the manager a file that needs no
re-walk.
- Keep the associates moving without redoing
their work.
- Design the sample and assign items.
- Trace samples to evidence, clear the hard
ones herself.
- Raise and resolve exceptions with the
client.
- Draft conclusions and prepare for review.
Workpaper system, Document request portal,
Spreadsheets for tracking, Email and chat with
the client
Knows the procedure cold. Knows which client
contact answers which request. Does not need
guidance; needs speed.
- Three systems opened to find one statement.
- Review waits, then notes loop.
- Re-walking the sample for the manager
because the file does not hold the state.
Owns the fieldwork result. If the file is late
or thin, it is her name the manager says
first.
Retrieval, extraction and the field-by-field
matching. 'It can do the matching. I will look
at the differences.'
Deciding what an exception means. Talking to
the client about it.
Seeing the page it read, next to the field it
extracted. Being able to rerun one step with
the right file.
Eight years. Reviews for five engagements in the
same weeks.
Mostly office or home. Review happens in
blocks between client meetings, often late.
- Clear review queues before the partner needs
the file.
- Catch the reference and format problems
early so they do not reach the partner.
- Know, at a glance, what is waiting on whom.
- Review workpapers and raise notes.
- Judge exception resolutions.
- Decide what escalates to the partner.
- Coach seniors through notes.
Workpaper system review mode, Email for notes
outside the system, A personal list of what is
waiting
Reads a workpaper by its references first.
Knows which seniors need a second look.
- Layout differs per team, so decoding
precedes judging.
- Notes cleared then reopened.
- No view of the whole queue across
engagements.
Signs the review. Shares the consequence of
anything the partner finds later.
Drafting with references in place. Flagging
exceptions with the evidence attached.
The review decision itself. 'A number alone is
not confidence.'
Step-level visibility. Rejecting one step
without discarding the run. Knowing the agent
could not read restricted material without a
checkpoint.
Nineteen years. Signs for a portfolio of
engagements.
Travelling between clients. Reads on a laptop
in short windows. Signs when the file is
ready, not when it is convenient.
- Sign a file she could defend to an inspector
a year later.
- See the exception trail before the
conclusion.
- Spend her attention on judgment, not on
format.
- Final review of high-risk areas.
- Decide on misstatements and waivers.
- Sign off.
- Answer for the file afterward.
Workpaper system summary views, The manager's
verbal walkthrough
Pattern-matches across engagements. Knows
which exceptions become findings.
- The exception trail is spread across
workpapers and emails.
- Being asked to sign before the review is
complete.
- Not knowing what a tool did with the
client's data.
Personal liability. Independence. 'If it is
wrong, it is still my name.'
Assembly of the evidence trail. Consistency
checks across workpapers.
Conclusions. Sign-off. Anything that writes
into the file as final.
A human checkpoint before anything restricted
was read. A visible record of what the agent
did, in the file, not in a log.
Twelve years in audit, four in methodology.
Firm office. Works across engagements, not
inside one. Writes the rules teams work to.
- Rules that teams can follow without
memorizing them.
- Structures that fit procedures so teams stop
adapting them by hand.
- A file that can be re-performed from its
contents.
- Maintain the Test of Details structures.
- Set documentation and checkpoint rules.
- Review quality findings across engagements.
- Answer teams' methodology questions.
Methodology library, Quality review tooling,
Structure templates
Knows every structure and why each field
exists. Knows where teams deviate and what it
costs.
- Local variants of standard structures.
- Data handling rules known unevenly.
- Reviewing rules in documents nobody reads
under pressure.
Answers for methodology compliance across the
practice.
Planning a run against a typed structure.
Enforcing data classes. Documenting steps
consistently.
Changing a structure or a rule without
methodology review.
The agent plans against the library, not
around it. Checkpoints are rules in the
product, not guidance in a document.

svg.text: Anti-persona: the auditor who routes around the tool

text.tspan: Fast, competent, keeps a personal tracker because the
systems never held the state he needed. Trusts his own
spreadsheet over any tool that slows him down or hides what
it did.
- Any step that adds a click without adding
certainty.
- Any output he cannot check in seconds.
- Any tool that makes the risk his while
keeping the work invisible.
- Copies data out to a spreadsheet.
- Approves agent output without opening the
source.
- Reruns the whole run instead of fixing one
step.

svg.text: WHAT THE DESIGN DOES ABOUT IT

text.tspan: - Keyboard-first density so the product is
faster than the spreadsheet (D-15).
- Citation chips that make checking faster
than trusting (D-03).
- Step-level rejection and rerun so fixing
is cheaper than discarding (D-14).
- The run holds the state he used to keep in
his head (D-13).

svg.text: Composite and reconstructed. Each persona is a composite built from the themes in 03. No attribute carries an observation, participant or quote count. Names are invented.
